I was talking to my kid the other day.

I was explaining to her why you get in trouble if you say certain things. I told her that they change what is the polite way to say stuff, and you have to keep up with which word is the polite word or you get in trouble. For example, it used to be just fine to say "retarded", but now you have to say "on the autism spectrum". It used to be fine to say "colored" but now you have to say "people of color." I told her if you say the wrong thing, (((people))) assume you are low-class and you get held back from opportunities in life. I said it is OK to talk like that around /us/ but not around (((them))).

Then it occurred to me that this happened at least once before. All of our current English language vulgarity comes from the Norman Conquest. Before the conquest, Anglo-Saxon words like "shit" and "fuck" were not vulgar. After the conquest, you had to say Norman French words like "excrement" and "have sex" or you were low class . . . and it goes even further, as the perfectly good words for cows and sheep were relegated to the low-class people who tended them, while the high-class people who ate them used Norman French words like beef and mutton.

So language used as a way to distinguish social classes is a symptom of conquest. We have been conquered and are occupied.
